A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TusoAI, with matching methods, benchmarks, and genetics applications. Text, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched despite extensive appendix additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component and backbone ablations, and simulation and real-data results for scDRS and pgBoost.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds literature-sensitivity experiments, efficiency analyses, and a warm-start NinaPro experiment.

M1.justification: The core TusoAI procedure remains unchanged, but Appendix O introduces an evaluated variant with optional paper-summary filtering, a limited addition to literature processing whose filtering rule is unspecified. Algorithm 1 also corrects diagnostic initialization to match the predefined instructions already described in v1; this is not a new diagnostic mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six single-cell tasks, five scientific deep-learning tasks, and two genetics applications. Warm-start NinaPro changes initialization within an existing task. The generic classification example in v2 Appendix V is illustrative, not an additional evaluated task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in Tables 1–3 and the genetics comparisons. Appendix F supplies names, descriptions, and citations for existing expert baselines rather than establishing replacements. The new warm-start NinaPro comparison reuses the existing NinaPro comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the experimental design with controls for 0, 10, and 50 retrieved papers, filtered versus unfiltered summaries, and 5-, 15-, and 30-point summaries. Appendix T adds an eight-hour NinaPro optimization initialized from the expert model. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and standard optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to literature quantity, filtering, and summary length; relate diversity persistence to optimization convergence; report broader TusoAI and AIDE trajectories; and examine runtime and cost. Appendix T adds a warm-start case study with identified optimization steps. These substantially extend v1's component, backbone, and genetics analyses.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three-seed confidence intervals and replicate stability. v2 adds five-replicate score distributions for the component ablations and reports five replicates for literature-sensitivity tests. Table 2 also supplies the previously missing AMBER/DeepSEA uncertainty term. This does not establish that the original three-seed benchmarks were expanded to five runs.

E6.justification: The point estimates and rankings in Tables 1–3 and the principal genetics findings are retained. Substantial new results include warm-start NinaPro scoring 0.94 versus the expert model's 0.91, a diversity-persistence/convergence correlation of 0.519, and literature-sensitivity, runtime, cost, and trajectory results. The NinaPro finding uses a different initialization, not an improved score under the original cold-start setting.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation and multiplicative category-update rule are unchanged. The new symbol glossary and Bayesian-style interpretation explain existing mathematics; neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about structured domain knowledge, adaptive planning, diagnostic optimization, benchmark performance, and genetics discoveries remain. v2 condenses numerical examples in the abstract and contribution list without materially changing the claims retained in Sections 4–5.

C2.justification: The new Discussion explicitly identifies dependence on fast, representative validation experiments; limitations when methods span multiple functions; inherited weaknesses of existing evaluators; and heuristic components lacking theoretical justification. v2 also develops the interpretation of diversity in search and warm-start complementarity with expert models, substantially expanding the account of applicability and limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix U newly provides prompts for implementation, instruction-based optimization, diagnostic generation and use, feedback, and debugging. v2 also expands expert-baseline specifications, identifies API access routes, supplies task-construction examples, clarifies pgBoost discovery thresholds, and reports runtime and cost information. These materially improve documentation of retained procedures.

R1.justification: New Appendix H substantially develops novelty positioning against ALRA and DenoiseIt, coordinate- and graph-based spatial-gene methods, and restricted NAS search spaces. Numerous supporting references and expert-method citations are added. Section 1.1 also sharpens the distinction from prior systems through function-level optimization without requiring existing models.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract and contribution list, adds a Discussion and acknowledgments, clarifies terminology and cross-references, and rewrites prompt listings into more readable templates. Most existing main-text prose and its narrative sequence remain intact; much of the expansion is additional scientific or technical content.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual material for trajectories, efficiency, literature sensitivity, diversity/convergence, and warm-start performance, plus a symbol table and example tables. Existing figures receive revised labels, legends, captions, and positioning; Figure 2 replaces connected candidate scores with scatter points. Prompt and code appendices are extensively reformatted into styled boxes and lists.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves scrutiny and reproducibility by supplying previously missing optimization-loop prompts, testing literature-use choices, and reporting replicated ablations and efficiency evidence. Its explicit limitations also better delimit the retained claims. These address important documentation and validation gaps in v1, although the new summary-filtering procedure remains underspecified and the headline benchmark scores are unchanged.
